correctness.rationale: The fixed-size ODE is exactly the normalization of (3.3) and (3.4) stated in the record, with g'(0)=1, R0=1, and Jacobian rows (−1/2,1/2), (1,−1). The matching plus two s-sets realizes the claimed regular hypergraph. The square is forward invariant, and strict positivity at finite times follows, e.g., from x'≥−x and y'≥−y inside it. For V=x+y/2, 2V'=f−x−x²−(x+f)y; f≤x, and only the origin can stay on x=0, so LaSalle gives extinction. The arctangent remainder implies −KV²≤V'≤0. For z'=−a(t)z+O(V^j), a(t)≥a0>0 eventually, setting w=z/V^j gives w'=(−a−j V'/V)w+O(1), whose linear coefficient is eventually at most −a0/2 since V→0. Thus z=O(V^j), independently validating the slow-variation estimate. Subtracting the ODEs gives d'=−(3+x)d/2+(f−x)(1−x−d) for d=y−x. Apply the estimate with j=3, giving d=O(V³) and x∼2V/3. With A=−2s²/9 the cubic term of (d−Ax³)' cancels and the remaining forcing is O(x⁴); the same estimate gives d=Ax³+O(x⁴). Therefore u=1/x has u'=1+s²/(9u)+O(u⁻²), first u∼t, then u=t+O(log t). Subtracting the printed logarithm leaves an integrable derivative O(log t/t²), proving a finite intercept for every strict interior start and the difference-of-sizes limit. The submitted symbolic/finite-time checks were inspected, not executed, and are not used as asymptotic proof.
